description: Input is everything sent (system prompt, history, tools, documents); output is everything generated, including hidden reasoning tokens. Output usually costs several times more.
Input tokens plus `maxTokens` of output, priced before the call. The only estimate that can guarantee a budget.
A fraction added to a local token estimate (rounded up) so it still bounds the provider's count when the model's tokenizer differs from yours. Pick it from measured drift.
The gap between your local token count and the provider's reported usage. Measure it on real traffic by comparing estimates with `usage`.
The provider's own token and cost counts after the call. What you record, bill and alert on; the estimate is only for the decision to send.
Limits per request, per session or task, per user and per feature. Each is checked before the request leaves the process.
Prefill reads the input and sets time to first token; decode generates output one token at a time and usually dominates total latency.
The latency 95% of calls stay under. Users remember slow calls, so set targets on percentiles, not averages.
A `now()` function passed in instead of reading the system time directly, so latency logic can be tested without waiting.
